title: Knowledge Check 7 - Lessons 31-35
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 31-35 - Data Management. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: Three downstream systems must react within seconds whenever an Opportunity stage changes, and the customer does not want each one polling Salesforce. Which design fits?
options: A nightly batch export that each system downloads
A synchronous REST call from Salesforce to each system on save
Change Data Capture or a Platform Event that publishes the change and lets the three systems subscribe
A shared spreadsheet refreshed hourly
questions.explanation: An event driven design publishes the change once and lets interested subscribers react in near real time, which is exactly what Change Data Capture and Platform Events are built for, while polling loads the org with needless requests.

questions.question: A company must move 40 million historical order lines into Salesforce every night. Which integration shape is correct?
options: A synchronous REST call per order line
An asynchronous batch job on Bulk API 2.0
A single SOAP call with all the lines in the payload
A manual Data Loader run each night
questions.explanation: Very large scheduled volume is asynchronous work, and Bulk API 2.0 processes the job server side without holding a synchronous request open, which is why it is the right shape.

questions.question: Six systems share customer data and each currently calls the others directly. Change requests are slow and there is no single place to see integration failures. What is the best design?
options: Introduce a middleware layer that each system talks to instead of calling each other
Add more point to point connections with better logging
Move all the data into a single nightly flat file
Have each system poll Salesforce every minute
questions.explanation: Middleware centralizes the mapping, transformation, retry, and monitoring in one hub, replacing a growing mesh of point to point connections and giving one place to observe failures.

questions.question: A report on a multi million row custom object times out, and its filter uses a field that is not indexed. What is the most direct scalability fix?
options: Add more fields to the report
Make the filter selective and use an indexed field, requesting a custom index on that field if none exists
Increase the page size of the report
Move the object to a different org
questions.explanation: Make the filter selective and indexed, requesting a custom index on that field if none exists. A non indexed filter forces a table scan, and adding fields or changing page size does nothing about the scan.

questions.question: A customer filters a large object constantly on a field that is not indexed, and also runs reports that read a small set of hot fields from the same object. Which two features address these?
options: A duplicate rule and a validation rule
Sharing rules and org wide defaults
A custom index on the filtered field and a skinny table for the hot fields
A scheduled dashboard and a report folder
questions.explanation: A custom index speeds the filtered queries, and a skinny table, which is a Support created copy of the most used fields, speeds the reads of the hot fields.

questions.question: An admin edits the role hierarchy on an org whose largest object holds tens of millions of records. What scalability consequence should the consultant warn about?
options: The records are permanently deleted
Sharing recalculation for the affected records can run for a long time and should be scheduled into a maintenance window
The API limits reset immediately
All reports are deleted
questions.explanation: Changing the hierarchy triggers sharing recalculation across affected records, and at tens of millions of rows that recalculation is expensive, so it belongs in a maintenance window rather than in the middle of the business day.

questions.question: A sales org plans to keep seven years of activity and email history on millions of opportunity records. What scalability implication and response should the consultant raise?
options: The records will be deleted automatically by Salesforce
Data storage grows against the edition's licensed limit, so a retention and archiving policy should move old records to an external store
Activity records do not count toward storage
Storage can be increased without limit for free
questions.explanation: Activity and email history consume licensed data storage, so keeping seven years on millions of records requires a retention and archiving policy to move the tail out of Salesforce.

questions.question: A design gives precise access through a deep role hierarchy and dozens of ownership based sharing rules over tens of millions of records. What is the scalability implication?
options: There is none, because sharing rules are free
The deployment will fail to compile
Sharing recalculation becomes expensive, so the sharing model should be as simple as the security requirement allows and hierarchy changes batched into maintenance windows
The API limit doubles
questions.explanation: A deep hierarchy with many sharing rules means more to compute and recalculate, and each change to the hierarchy triggers recalculation across affected records, so simplifying the model and batching changes are the scalability responses.

questions.question: A bulk recalculation must update two million opportunity records when a product's price changes. Which processing choice scales?
options: A synchronous trigger on the price object that updates every opportunity in one transaction
Asynchronous Apex, using Batch Apex to chunk the two million records, with Queueable for chained follow up work
A user manually editing the records
A single Data Loader run done while the business is live
questions.explanation: Two million records exceeds what a single synchronous transaction can handle, so asynchronous Apex, chunked with Batch and chained with Queueable, is the scalable choice.

questions.question: A sales operations lead reports that roughly 30 percent of open Opportunities have a blank Amount and a blank Close Date, and the forecast is unreliable. Which data quality dimension is failing, and what is the most direct first control?
options: Uniqueness, so enable duplicate rules on Opportunity
Completeness, so make Amount and Close Date required and enforce it with a validation rule
Validity, so convert Amount and Close Date to restricted picklists
Timeliness, so shorten the data stream refresh interval
questions.explanation: Blank values in required business fields are a completeness failure, and the direct control is making the fields required at the object level rather than only on the page layout. The other options name real dimensions but none of them fixes a missing value.

questions.question: A customer deploying Agentforce complains that the agent routes to the wrong Account and quotes from stale pricing. The consultant traces both to CRM records. What is the correct framing to give the customer?
options: The agent needs a larger language model
Agent quality is bounded by CRM data quality, so the duplicate Accounts and stale Price Book entries must be fixed first
The agent needs its own separate data store
Prompt engineering will compensate for the underlying records
questions.explanation: Agents grounded in Salesforce inherit the state of the CRM, so duplicate Accounts and stale Price Book entries surface as agent errors. Framing this as a model or prompt problem defers a data problem that will keep recurring.

questions.question: A compliance officer asks two things: prove who changed an Opportunity Amount six months ago, and satisfy a new policy requiring ten years of retention. What is the correct recommendation?
options: Standard Field History Tracking covers both, because its retention is indefinite
Export the Opportunity table to a spreadsheet archive every month
Enable Field History Tracking for the six month need and Field Audit Trail for the ten year policy, noting that Field Audit Trail access is API only and needs a Shield or Field Audit Trail license
Turn on Debug Logs for all users and retain the log files
questions.explanation: Standard tracking retains only 18 to 24 months and caps at 20 fields per object, so the ten year policy requires Field Audit Trail, which archives to FieldHistoryArchive, retains until deleted, and is API only. A spreadsheet export is not an audit trail, and Debug Logs are not a field history.

questions.question: An admin imports 200,000 Accounts with Data Loader and finds hundreds of duplicates that the Salesforce UI would have blocked. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The matching rule was deleted before the import
Data Loader does not enforce duplicate rules unless that option is explicitly enabled
Duplicate rules apply only to Leads and Contacts
The import ran under a user without Modify All Data
questions.explanation: Duplicate rules fire on UI and API save paths, but Data Loader skips them unless the option is enabled, which is why a governed org can still import duplicates in bulk.

questions.question: A customer wants to stop duplicate Contacts at the point of entry but still allow an occasional legitimate near match to be saved with a warning. Which configuration meets both requirements?
options: A matching rule set to Block
A duplicate rule with a Block action and a narrow matching rule
A duplicate rule with an Allow and report action, paired with a matching rule tuned for fuzzy and blank handling
A validation rule on the Email field
questions.explanation: Allowing the save with a report gives the warning and the Duplicate Record Set work queue, while the matching rule must be tuned so the near matches are actually detected. Blocking would prevent the legitimate saves the customer wants to keep.

questions.question: An integration writes Opportunities every night and must bypass the new Amount validation rule, while sales users must not be able to. What is the correct approach?
options: Remove the validation rule and rely on training
Keep the validation rule and scope a bypass to the integration user through a custom permission or hierarchy setting the rule checks
Move Amount to required on the page layout
Have the integration write with the Data Import Wizard instead
questions.explanation: Validation rules are the layer that actually protects the object, so keep it and give the trusted integration a controlled bypass. Removing it or downgrading to a page layout requirement would leave the data unprotected.
